title: Into the Eagle's Nest
build: PAL cassette, Pandora, inlay stamped 1986, analysed at the loader's hand-over

tools.host: Linux 6.6 x86_64 (WSL2) on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Ubuntu 26.04, Intel x86_64, display through WSLg
tools.emulator: own build of github.com/barryw/vice-mcp, release v3.13.2, commit 1e83aab134; driven through kit/c64/vice.py; check-emulator 57 of 57
tools.publication: Python 3 and node 24; symbols_export.py, listing.py and build.py

accuracy.note: the music driver, which took the tune's first notes a tick late where the game takes them in the same call
every one of the 13 was read against the code again and held; an audit is recommended

the chests, the shot and the tape: open chests put in front of the player in the game, a shot followed frame by frame, and the tape image decoded by the loader's rules, after the contributor questioned the chest odds
the chest widget's odds, checked against tables built by the game's own loop with the sound chip running
and every claim in facts.md, 28 of 114 corrected; made on the contributor's run, not by a maintainer
after the audit, by a checker that took no part in it; made on the contributor's run, not by a maintainer
the comments again, by five new checkers told the kinds of error found; made on the contributor's run, not by a maintainer
after the second audit, by a checker that took no part in it; made on the contributor's run, not by a maintainer
the whole game ported routine by routine and held in lockstep with its own code; 14 comments the port showed wrong were corrected

exclude: runtime: the screen, which the game fills with tiles and the status panel; the bytes the loader left here are its own loading screen
runtime: the sprite pointers and the bytes beside them, written at the start of every mission
runtime: the figures' positions on the floor, filled in by the map builder at $6A40 as it reads the floor's description
runtime: the figures' places in the castle map and their kinds, filled in by the map builder
runtime: the 256 random bytes $67CA reads out of the sound chip's noise oscillator at start-up
runtime: the buffer the message printer at $5935 fills with the characters of the line being shown
runtime: untouched at the hand-over, inside the map builder's working area
runtime: the top quarter of the castle map, built from the floor's description by $6A40
runtime: the bottom part of the castle map, built from the floor's description by $6A40
untouched RAM beneath the KERNAL, apart from the two bytes at $FFFE the load wrote; no instruction in the game names any of it
extra: the title picture's bitmap, loaded from tape and shown while the rest of the tape loads; the castle map is built over it once the game runs
include: the four floors' descriptions, a kilobyte each, which the game reads with the I/O area banked out

regions: the play screen's character set: the castle's tiles, the figures, the pickups, the panel's letters and the digits
the big alphabet the attract screens and the message line are written in, two cells by two to a character
the sprite shapes: the player's twelve poses of four, the flash at the barrel's four and the castle on the panel
the 33 messages for the line at the bottom of the screen
the blocks the castle's floors are built from, four tiles by four
the colour of each tile of the play character set
the title picture's screen colours, which the video chip reads while the tape loads and no instruction does
the title picture's bitmap, which the castle map is built over
the four floors' descriptions, a kilobyte each
the stone plaque's bitmap and its colours
